title: The decoder computes a negative output length for a padded tail, and the negative becomes a full-width store
index_line: T-0095 · MEM_WRITE · OpenJDK Base64 intrinsic: stray '=' → negative tail length → 64-byte store into a 50-byte buffer · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: An optimised decoder assumes the remaining output length for a padded group is a small non-negative number: the tail is handled with a mask derived from how many bytes are left. A malformed input makes that count negative, and a negative count converted to a SIMD store mask is not 'no store' — it is every lane.

mechanism.does: attacker-supplied Base64 text (64 payload characters followed by a single '=') reaches a decoding path that uses java.util.Base64
after the function is invoked repeatedly the JIT compiles it and the HotSpot x86-64 Base64 intrinsic handles the decode
the tail handler computes the output length for the padded group, mishandles the stray '=', and derives a negative length
the negative length becomes a full 64-byte store mask against a 50-byte result array, writing 62 bytes past the end with an attacker-chosen constant
with heap shaping, a neighbouring array's length is corrupted and its data copied back into the response — a heap disclosure primitive
the bounded constant write is escalated to arbitrary writes that reach the code cache and JVM hooks, yielding code execution

source.http.request.value: Base64 text carried in a request (remember-me cookie, Authorization header, form field, message payload)

sink.memory.copy.value: the intrinsic's masked vector store into the decode result buffer

size.length.value: the tail output length that goes negative and is reinterpreted as a full-width store mask

encoding.string.value: Base64 with a padded tail — the encoding whose padding rule the optimised tail handler special-cases

preconditions.expr: the JVM runs an affected build on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 VBMI
a request path reaches java.util.Base64 decoding of attacker-influenced data
the decode path is reachable before authentication in the deployed application

check.spec: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://HOST/; printf 'probe the endpoint that carries Base64 input (cookie/header/form)\n'

success: a heap disclosure in the response after the 65-byte input (64 payload + '=')
JVM crash with a corrupted object header/array length adjacent to a decode buffer
failure_like: the JVM is patched, ARM64-only, or the CPU lacks AVX-512 VBMI (the intrinsic is not used)
the value is rejected before reaching the intrinsic
false_positive: invalid Base64 errors are normal and prove nothing — require the negative-tail path (exact 64+1 shape) and heap effects
a crash without a disclosure or controlled write is not this record's mechanism

hazards: hand-rolled SIMD tail handlers: the mask derived from a remaining-count is the classic signedness trap
the write value is a constant, so the attacker controls location more than content — heap shaping does the rest
intrinsics bypass the safety expectations of the language method they implement
non_transfers: scalar implementations or builds without the AVX-512 VBMI intrinsic
padded-tail handlers that clamp the remaining count to zero

evidence.target: OpenJDK HotSpot x86-64 Base64 intrinsic (CVE-2026-114938, Java4Shell), affected Oracle Java SE / GraalVM builds

provenance.author: Calif.io (Quang Luong)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-114938 Java4Shell: the HotSpot x86-64 Base64 intrinsic miscalculates the padded tail store mask; 64 A characters plus a stray = produce a negative output length that becomes a full 64-byte write, 62 bytes past a 50-byte array; heap feng shui turns the constant write into a heap disclosure (JavaBleed) and RCE; pre-auth RCE demonstrated in Jenkins and Keycloak, post-auth in Elasticsearch; requires AVX-512 VBMI

provenance.author: Apache Shiro Team
provenance.corroborates: independent impact analysis: the flaw is in the OpenJDK HotSpot Base64 decoder, not Shiro; Shiro applications are exposed where a request path reaches java.util.Base64 — notably CookieRememberMeManager decoding the remember-me cookie; exploitation depends on the JDK, AVX-512 VBMI support, and reaching the decoder

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-114938 description, affected Java SE/GraalVM versions

provenance.author: OpenJDK Vulnerability Group
provenance.corroborates: vendor advisory for the November 2026 CPU including CVE-2026-114938
